reviews.text: The mere fact that the film can tell the story of an at times tortured artist like Elton John while still managing to have its audience tap their feet and sing-a-long to some of his most recognisable tunes is a feat upon itself.
reviews.author: David Griffiths

reviews.text: It’s a deeply personal film, and its willingness to showcase such reflection, instead of demanding sympathy, demonstrates a level of humbleness that’s hard not to lose yourself in, even without the radiant visuals.
reviews.author: Calum Cooper

reviews.text: …with Elton John very much alive, still standing and able to approve all creative choices, the result is a fun if rather self-regarding look at a great musician and performer…
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: Throughout all of these musical moments and dramatic tension, two things remain, the visual style of Fletcher and the best performance of Taron Edgerton’s career.
reviews.author: Ryan McQuade

reviews.text: Rocketman managed to deliver an authentic biopic that wasn’t afraid to take risks.
reviews.author: Nicolas Soto

reviews.text: Using the pop superstar and gay icon’s own music, director Dexter Fletcher leads audiences on a fantastic journey through Elton John’s early life...
reviews.author: Brian T. Carney

reviews.text: A colorful exploration of John’s illustrious career, the film boldly addressed his many past addictions (with sex, drugs, and alcohol) while also functioning as an actual musical with huge setpieces and real-life singing...
reviews.author: Michael Cuby

reviews.text: Rocketman is a strong, triumphant look at the life and times of singer Elton John. Taron Egerton gives an astounding, emotional, and electric performance as the legendary pop star.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Harris

reviews.text: A bold, dazzling, lavish, decadent film that features a career-altering performance by Taron Egerton.
reviews.author: M.N. Miller

reviews.text: Taron Egerton’s performance, including pitch-perfect singing, is nothing short of miraculous. He’s energetic, egomaniacal, and yet somehow thoroughly worth empathizing with.
reviews.author: Merryn Johns

reviews.text: Rocketman is, in some ways, a sad reminder that even in its most supposedly fantastic imaginings, Hollywood fantasies can still be so straight.
reviews.author: Alessa Dominguez

reviews.text: The committed performance is something speciala sensitive and frenzied role that reminds us just how fascinating Elton John and his music remains.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: While Rocketman follows specific musical bio-pic structures, its choice to turn the sub-genre upside down with its style shows homage to not only the man but his eternal impact on music.
reviews.author: David Gonzalez

reviews.text: Episode 38: Brightburn / The Perfection / Rocketman
reviews.author: Taylor Baker

reviews.text: I was very pleasantly surprised... it's bombastic but [Edgerton] handles it very well.
reviews.author: Lonita Cook

reviews.text: Rocketman is nothing less than sheer joy, which uses every filmic trick in cinema's arsenal to serve up a smorgasbord of feel-good delights.
reviews.author: Ben Turner

reviews.text: Though dealing with familiar issues, Rocketman takes off with more intense energy than most movies about popular music stars.
reviews.author: Robin Holabird

reviews.text: Rocketman transcends its well-worn form with beautifully executed flights of fantasy that encapsulate the carefree joy of song.
reviews.author: Yasmin Omar

reviews.text: Taron Egerton is nothing short of a revelation.
reviews.author: Nicolás Delgadillo

reviews.text: Taron Egerton stars as the iconic pop star in a movie-musical that doesn't shy away from showing us Elton's dark side.
reviews.author: Nick Levine

reviews.text: A musical simply bursting with the joy of existing.
reviews.author: Olly Richards

reviews.text: A giddy yet sobering film that is part chronological biopic and part musical fantasy that's bound to have fans tapping their feet.
reviews.author: Jason Fraley

reviews.text: An insulting movie ... desperately groping for some semblance of autobiography.
reviews.author: Michael J. Casey

reviews.text: Showing how fantastical the ups and downs of fame, fortune and rock stardom can be by sashaying through a sea of surreality, the result is a winning marriage of form and feeling.
reviews.author: Sarah Ward

reviews.text: Rocketman doesn't follow the conventions of most music biopics, and it's all the better for it.
reviews.author: Alex Bentley

reviews.text: ... a lot better than it probably has a right to be.
reviews.author: Fletcher Powell

reviews.text: Glittering eye candy with much humanity on display.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: I recommend Rocketman to audiences that are fans of musicals, emotional journeys, and movies about real-life people. It's one of the best movies of the year, and deservingly so.
reviews.author: Shah Shahid

reviews.text: In the leading role, Taron Egerton absolutely shone as Elton. The fact he actually sang so many of his iconic songs, and did them well, is something that should be celebrated for years to come.
reviews.author: Lucy Buglass

reviews.text: It's a majestic ode to the beloved icon with directorial flair.
reviews.author: Matthew St. Clair

reviews.text: Glory and fame always come at a price [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Gisela Savdie

reviews.text: In its music, drama, romance and fantasy, it never forgets the human side of the icon from which it's telling the story. Magnificent film. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Victor Pineyro

reviews.text: Whatever Rocketman' s shortcomings, or its subject's, the film is an exhilarating ride and a reminder of why so much of Elton John's music is appealing and enduring.
reviews.author: Joanne Laurier

reviews.text: It is a purely conventional, predictable and frivolous biopic that barely brushes the surface of the protagonist. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: In the context of Elton John's life, many of his songs take on extra meaning. The result feels fantastical and edges into the realm of magical realism; if that wasn't built to tell Elton John's story, I don't know what was.
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: The film works best when it's too fast for its hero. It's frustrating, then, that it's too fast for itself as well.
reviews.author: Matt Cipolla

reviews.text: Dexter Fletcher gives a duly reverent and indulgent treatment of a man who confounds a culture still trying to define him.
reviews.author: Prahlad Srihari

reviews.text: Even as the film is every bit as flashy and ebullient as the man it celebrates, it falls disappointingly short - certainly to a far greater extent than last year's Bohemian Rhapsody did - of being a rounded portrait of a life and a career.
reviews.author: Saibal Chatterjee

reviews.text: Rocketman takes the traditional musical idea of songs being the outward expression of a character's inner thoughts and allows us a deep dive into the mind of this artistic genius.
reviews.author: Damond Fudge

reviews.text: Elton John's robust rockers and heartfelt earnest songs all get their proper due in tonally perfect context.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: Good performances, fun songs.
reviews.author: Avaryl Halley

reviews.text: It was fine.
reviews.author: Andrew Galdi

reviews.text: Despite existing in a fantasy world, these characters are unmistakably human, and that, along with the masterful film craft on display, is what makes this one of the best musical biopics ever made.
reviews.author: Dan Scully

reviews.text: It's Taron Egerton as Elton John who carries and sells the film -- often backwards and in platform heels. Wild as it may sound to approach such a mercurial and marvelous character with beautiful restraint, Egerton's performance is meticulously calibrated.
reviews.author: Erin Keane

reviews.text: What makes Rocketman so uneven is, ironically enough, a lack of understanding of what makes Elton John so iconic.
reviews.author: Marshall Estes

reviews.text: Dexter Fletcher's Elton John biopic is an entertaining if imperfect film with a fantastic performance from Taron Egerton.
reviews.author: Mina Takla

reviews.text: A bright and colorful telling of a rock icon's life that shows off the ups and downs in splendorific fashion.
reviews.author: Julian Lytle

reviews.text: There's a sense of craftsmanship that gives Rocketman a step above other biopics that have the same story beats.
reviews.author: Damian Levy

reviews.text: With Rocketman, the young star Taron Egerton showcases incredible talent. Shockingly, Rocketman might live up to the promise of an Elton John biopic.
reviews.author: Alan French

reviews.text: This is a very sentimental film - but then isn't that the pleasure of musicals? I'm here for Rocketman's exuberant mythologising.
reviews.author: Mel Campbell

reviews.text: Elton John puts it all out there, and Taron Egerton is "Captain Fantastic" as Elton John.
reviews.author: Paul McGuire Grimes

reviews.text: Rocketman forgoes the biopic element for entertainment as Fletcher includes lots of unnecessary visual elements, hiding the man behind the performer.
reviews.author: Katie Smith-Wong

reviews.text: The movie not only does a fine job in finding the emotionally and narratively meaningful moments for the songs, but also reminds you what power lies in the magical combination of music and lyrics itself.
reviews.author: Zhuo-Ning Su

reviews.text: Dexter Fletcher has reinvigorated the musical biopic.
reviews.author: Karen M. Peterson

reviews.text: Rocketman ramps the camp up to 11, throws on some sequinned spectacles, and sparks fireworks of pure joy in glitzy song-and-dance routines.
reviews.author: Rebecca Harrison

reviews.text: Sometimes it feels just a little contrived, but it has a freeness and a lightness and a sort of Bollywood-ness to it that is a lot of fun to watch.
reviews.author: Lael Loewenstein

reviews.text: If only the film's unflinching gaze and sheer energy were enough to inspire a great film.
reviews.author: Jason Di Rosso

reviews.text: While Dexter Fletcher attempts spectacle in his set pieces, he lacks the charm and technical prowess to nail them successfully.
reviews.author: Juan Barquin

reviews.text: When I say Rocketman is not your typical biopic, I mean it is not your typical biopic. A mix of real life events and fantasy -- and trust me when I say, it works perfectly.
reviews.author: Tessa Smith

reviews.text: This is certainly not your typical biopic but rather an entertaining mix of real-life and fantasy - much like Elton John is himself.
reviews.author: Allison Rose

reviews.text: This is no countdown greatest hits album, this is something else entirely and I loved every single minute of it.
reviews.author: Kate Rodger

reviews.text: The film's framing device was a neat idea, though poorly executed...It wasn't a good sign that I spent much of Rocketman thinking about how incredibly talented and underused Jamie Bell is.
reviews.author: Alex Heeney

reviews.text: Full of great music and fantastical spectacle, "Rocketman" appears to be what everyone who found "Bohemian Rhapsody" lacking (I didn't - I thought it was one of the best films of the year) - wanted it to be.
reviews.author: Michael A. Smith

reviews.text: How wonderful life is, with Rocketman in the world.
reviews.author: Alan Cerny

reviews.text: Overall, Rocketman is a worthy portrayal of the life of one of our greatest living musical artists and gives Egerton an incredible spotlight role in his career. Pay attention, he's going to win an Oscar one day.
reviews.author: Karl Delossantos

reviews.text: This is the kind of stuff film buffs discuss over drinks, but for normal viewers, it can be tedious.
reviews.author: S. Indra Sathiabalan

reviews.text: We've all seen the biopic about the sad but talented little boy who finds fame and fortune before descending into a dark world of drink and drugs but you've never seen a film that blends fantasy, musical, and biopic so seamlessly...
reviews.author: Amelia Harvey

reviews.text: All biopics are fantasies of one kind or another; Rocketman has the daring to wear it on its cinematic sleeve.
reviews.author: James Kendrick

reviews.text: Rocketman is not the film that will send the genre into orbit. Its pleasures, however, are enough to give its audience a long-enough high.
reviews.author: Oggs Cruz

reviews.text: While, one suspects, Bohemian Rhapsody had [Freddie] Mercury weeping in his grave, the film of [Elton] John fits his life like an expensive sequinned glove.
reviews.author: Jonathan Dean

reviews.text: It is very engaging and has fantastic performances. Maybe a little bit too long and not quite as satisfying in the end.
reviews.author: Sean Chandler

reviews.text: The project serves as a terrific showcase for Egerton's clearly immense talent.
reviews.author: Sameen Amer

reviews.text: Rocketman makes it clear we are dealing with an exceptional artist... but it is not clear about who is the human being behind it. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Hugo Hernández Valdivia

reviews.text: Rocketman is far more than just a biopic. It's an experience.
reviews.author: Daniel Goodwin

reviews.text: Perhaps the best element of this musical is the fast paced choreographed dance moments combined with all of the cast breaking out into song at any given moment.
reviews.author: Sarah Knight Adamson

reviews.text: Rocketman, like its main actor, is vibrant. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Daniel Krauze

reviews.text: This is no impersonation of Elton, but it is a believable and credible interpretation that works stunningly well.
reviews.author: Graeme Tuckett

reviews.text: Still, it's a grand entertainment despite the traditional rise to fame - get messed up on drugs narrative.
reviews.author: Nathaniel Rogers

reviews.text: Rocketman is a solidly good film, but Elton John has lived a life of gigantic peaks and valleys. He deserves a film that compliments his life.
reviews.author: Tim Brennan

reviews.text: Rocketman isn't a sanitised peek-a-boo of someone's life, barely teasing at the surface of a complex creative genius. Rocketman gives you the warts and all version, and it's not going to pink-wash John's sexuality.
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: Part-biopic, part-musical and part-fantasy, Rocketman is an absolute blast.
reviews.author: Kong Rithdee

reviews.text: Big screen jukebox musical an enjoyably chaotic mess.
reviews.author: Sonny Bunch

reviews.text: Taron Egerton delivers. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: I liked it for the most part, and certain songs have been stuck in my head, but the cycle of repetition undermined it a bit. Still, a fantastic movie.
reviews.author: Martin Thomas

reviews.text: Nominate this, just to admit you made a mistake, this is what Bohemian Rhapsody should have been. This is exactly what we wanted.
reviews.author: Korey Coleman

reviews.text: Rocketman's tagline calls itself a "true fantasy", but it's the grounded elements that give it weight.
reviews.author: Joi Childs

reviews.text: It's fun and it's flashy but it's too hard to shake the shallowness and simplicity of the screenplay.
reviews.author: Matthew Toomey

reviews.text: Fletcher makes a perfect blend with the drama, the pain and the ecstasy of a musical. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fausto Ponce

reviews.text: Rocketman should thrill with its blast off, searing itself in our memory for hours or days after. But when the credits roll it's too much like another song from Sir Elton: "It's easier to walk away."
reviews.author: Andrew Kendall

reviews.text: Unique story with great musical numbers. Just wish it could have captured Elton's "Specialness".
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: One of the worst music biopics to come around in quite a while...
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: Bernie and Elton's relationship was cool, but there were many elements that they didn't show us...props to Taron Egerton for even tackling that.
reviews.author: Tony Baker

reviews.text: The result is a magical experience that is as vivacious and fearless as Elton John himself.
reviews.author: Courtney Small

reviews.text: This is a biography that falls into the trap of thinking that suffering is the same thing as depth.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: This film really works because of Taron Egerton's electrifying performance. And yes, that is him singing.
reviews.author: Joanne Soh

reviews.text: Egerton captures John's vocal style and manner in a way that goes beyond impersonation. He also does his own singing, unlike Rami Malek's Freddie Mercury in "Bohemian Rhapsody."
reviews.author: Loren King

reviews.text: Drugs, alcohol, sex, corrupt management, we've seen this all before, right? Not like this, we haven't. This musical biographical film about the early life of pop music star Elton John is presented in a highly imaginative way.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: Fantastic! Taron Egerton and director Dexter Fletcher deliver big time on everything I want from a musical biopic. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: In essence, Rocketman is a superficial game of hits from the first part of his career, well designed for the pleasure of his countless fans. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Leonardo Garcia Tsao

reviews.text: The film walks dangerously close to the edge of the melodrama or the annoying cliché of the "hard price of fame". [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Carlos Bonfil

reviews.text: Hindered by faulty construction and lax editing that tires out the audience long before its two-hour run time passes, "Rocketman" is nonetheless an energetic fantasy version of Elton John's incredible career in music.
reviews.author: Cole Smithey

reviews.text: Rocketman is a fantastical journey that makes you want to believe life is a musical.
reviews.author: Aisha Jordan

reviews.text: Really, on the basis of "Rocketman," you'd think Elton John never had a moment of fun.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: Egerton, Bell, the music, the camp, the spectacle, the costumes -- all strengths. The structure and the nuance regarding Elton's sexuality needed more finetuning, however.
reviews.author: Tomas Trussow

reviews.text: Elton's classic hits are used in a traditional musical way where the characters sing the words to tell the emotional story of how he got to rehab. I was singing but not jumping out of my seat since the actor doesn't have the vocal charisma of Elton.
reviews.author: Julia Swift

reviews.text: The momentum from the movie's first half dwindles to nothing.
reviews.author: Kristian M. Lin

reviews.text: Pompous in the presentation, Rocketman is not perfect, but had enough nerve to show Elton John flying during a performance at London's The Troubadour.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: In the musical biopic of Elton John, Rocketman drops the cinematic microphone... hard. Combining solid direction with a star-making performance from lead actor Taron Egerton, the movie is a diamond in the rough.
reviews.author: Kimberly Pierce

reviews.text: I can't imagine a better homage to one of the most important British artists that have ever lived. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: Even if it doesn't soar as high as one would like, Rocketman is still a better movie than Bohemian Rhapsody, which suffered in part from its PG-13 designation. Rocketman is a solid R, which is more in line for this sort of warts-and-all biopic.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: Don't expect anything more than a jukebox musical outlining the piano player's true-ish story.
reviews.author: Jay Horton

reviews.text: Like the Elton John it presents, it's about forgiveness. Love is love is love. Watching so many plume-festooned costumes take wing, you're inclined to believe that hope really is the thing with feathers.
reviews.author: Carrie Rickey

reviews.text: It's hard to pinpoint any real flaws in this movie...the movie is enlivened by its own approach.
reviews.author: Chris Stuckmann

reviews.text: The whole first half of the movie is awesome, seeing his family dynamic and how he learned music...I would probably watch it again, but there were a lot of problems. The directing was great and the cinematography was beautiful.
reviews.author: Steph Cozza

reviews.text: Hats off to [Fletcher for] his overall imaginative and colourful execution of Lee Hall's excellent script. Yet it would all have come to nought had its lead performance not been as moving, funny and powerful as Egerton's.
reviews.author: Paula Fleri-Soler

reviews.text: The musical numbers are grand, the acting is great and this is a must watch film for Elton John fans.
reviews.author: Jamal Grootboom

reviews.text: It's better than most music biopics, and not so much for what it has to say -- it's a fully authorized motion picture, after all -- but for the visual flair Fletcher brings to it.
reviews.author: Kathy Fennessy

reviews.text: Although it never really takes off like some great musical biopics, this crowd-pleasing odyssey affectionately captures the colorful flamboyance of its star while downplaying some of the more painful personal details.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: The biopic blueprint isn't overhauled in any major way, but with [Taron] Edgerton's confident performance and [Dexter] Fletcher's ability to weave a story from Elton's own beloved lyrics, Rocketman is a cosmic celebration of an unmatched talent.
reviews.author: Kiko Martinez

reviews.text: "Rocketman" is far from a drama of introspection-and, unfortunately, Egerton's performance, as directed by Fletcher, doesn't add to the protagonist's inner life.
reviews.author: Richard Brody

reviews.text: Fletcher captures the exhilarating spirit of those events, levitating the characters (and the audience) into a kind of phantasmagorical cinematic ecstasy.
reviews.author: Mattie Lucas

reviews.text: The result is insulting not only to the intelligence and taste of moviegoers, but to Elton John's legacy as a songwriter, showman, and immensely significant queer idol.
reviews.author: Morgan Troper

reviews.text: [It's] an unexpected performance by a relatively untried actor in the central role anchors Rocketman.
reviews.author: Steve Davis

reviews.text: He's round-faced and balding as Elton, with no Mr. Potatohead nose, but does a good job singing arrangements that diverge radically from the over-exposed originals.
reviews.author: Ken Eisner

reviews.text: Director Dexter Fletcher's energetically emotional musical is fantastically entertaining.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: Rocketman is many things: biography, comedy, drama, musical, and theater of the absurd. But above all, it is an honest testimony of the immense power of art in our lives. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge Rivera Rubio

reviews.text: Rocketman allows us to understand the construction and complexity of the character. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alfonso Flores-Durón y Martínez

reviews.text: The script is a hoard of showbiz clichés, and the tone ping-pongs between self-satisfaction and self-pity.
reviews.author: Rick Kisonak

reviews.text: This is the biopic of a queer rock icon we deserve.
reviews.author: Sarah Marrs

reviews.text: Rocketman is without a doubt a film that will enrapture with its music and its good feeling. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Israel Acosta Aroche

reviews.text: Glitzy, bold and rocking, Rocketman quickly shoots into the stratosphere and continues chasing the high through two hours of musical romps.
reviews.author: Jessica Rawden

reviews.text: A splash of colour and inspiration and a great central performance elevate Rocketman just beyond its stodgy, well-worn biopic structure.
reviews.author: Tom Augustine

reviews.text: Taron Egerton, his square jaw notwithstanding, throws body and soul into this origin story about the iconic British singer-performer.
reviews.author: Udita Jhunjhunwala

reviews.text: Rocketman  is a cannily honed machine, absolutely sure of its purpose, so you rather feel you've been sold a complete deluxe package... at times, consumer satisfaction is taken care of a little too aggressively for you to really feel involved.
reviews.author: Jonathan Romney

reviews.text: In case you weren't already in love with Taron Egerton, this movie will get you there.
reviews.author: Marianna Neal

reviews.text: I hope you don't mind that I put down in words how wonderful life is when Elton John's music, and this movie, are in the world.
reviews.author: Linda Cook

reviews.text: A brilliant joy. An astonishing rich, and indulgently fearless, curated life knitted beautifully together by director and star. It's got my Best Director, Best Actor nomination slots locked down.
reviews.author: Victoria Alexander

reviews.text: Egerton may not always hit the notes perfectly, and one or two songs feel a bit it's Elton John night on "American Idol," but he throws himself into every number. The result, often, is magical.
reviews.author: Ani Bundel

reviews.text: Rocketman is a better movie than Bohemian Rhapsody and [Taron] Egerton's performance as Elton John is better than [Rami] Malek's as Freddie Mercury.
reviews.author: Allen Adams

reviews.text: Extravagant and excessive, it's sparkly fun!
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: Even if it doesn't always quite hit the mark, and can get very cheesy, you come to admire its consistent, determined vision and boldness.
reviews.author: Deirdre Molumby

reviews.text: "Rocketman" is a big-hearted valentine that invites viewers to follow their passion. Corny, to be sure, but as summer entertainment goes, there's no denying it hits the sweet spot.
reviews.author: Rubén Rosario

reviews.text: It's the standard tale of rock 'n' roll excess leading to both loneliness and addiction, but the approach here is darkly introspective.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: The movie soars with its honest portrayal of Sir Elton, anchored by a show-stopping, where-did-that-come-from lead performance from Egerto.
reviews.author: Stephen Rebello

reviews.text: I liked Rocketman enough to give it a recommendation, but in the end, it felt like turning Elton John's music and life into a musical and the dark, recovery story cannibalized one another and lessened the overall film.
reviews.author: Alan Ng

reviews.text: That mysticism is combined perfectly thanks to the musical genre, which articulates tragedy with magic, catharsis and low blows with an exquisite rhythm that finds the synthesis in each letter of his songs. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Emiliano Basile

reviews.text: Something incredible has happened and I need to tell someone - Dexter Fletcher has made a great movie.
reviews.author: Ed Whitfield

reviews.text: It winds up as a big, warm, sometimes raunchy hug, with lots of catchy pop tunes.
reviews.author: Abbie Bernstein

reviews.text: An audiovisual show that further highlights Taron Egerton's incredible performance as the singer. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Abigail Camarillo

reviews.text: The choreographies work well as a counterpoint to what seeks to be historical reconstruction. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: William Venegas

reviews.text: Rocketman is flamboyant and rambunctious and everything Elton would be proud of. It's the musical biopic Bohemian Rhapsody wants to be when it grows up.
reviews.author: Matt Donato

reviews.text: Regardless of its shortcomings, the film's love of its subject matter is apparent, managing to help raise the predictable into something more daring and visually exciting than it has any right to be.
reviews.author: Allyson Johnson

reviews.text: Taron Egerton embodies Elton with his pitch-perfect singing and captivating natural presence. With this performance and the overall film, it's hard to imagine a better tribute to such a singular icon.
reviews.author: Oktay Ege Kozak

reviews.text: At its sequined core, "Rocketman" seems little more than a jukebox musical (a la "Jersey Boys"), dropping by the movie theaters en-route to its true home on Broadway.
reviews.author: Eleanor Ringel Cater

reviews.text: Taron Egerton shines as Elton John in one of the best musical biopics in recent memory.
reviews.author: Lauren Veneziani

reviews.text: If you really want to line (Bohemian Rhapsody) against (Rocketman), it's no contest - Rocketman is far and away the better film.
reviews.author: Matt Neal

reviews.text: By privileging the essence over accuracy, it is an emotional autobiography presented as a bizarre spectacle and camp. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fernanda Solórzano

reviews.text: Rocketman is an autobiographical film as deep as it is entertaining, with great performances and a magnificent production design. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Susana Guzman De la O

reviews.text: A magnificent feast of sex, drugs and rock & roll that leaves in diapers any of its recent counterparts. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Víctor López G.

reviews.text: Rocketman captures the fantasy and majesty of John's enduring legacy in a magical way, cranking up the tunes in a dream-hazed portrait that lives and breathes his identity.
reviews.author: Matt Ward

reviews.text: It's like sitting through a succession of riotous video clips punctuated by bouts of maudlin self-hatred.
reviews.author: John McDonald

reviews.text: 'Rocketman' is about the most ambitious and lavish musical biopic you'll find. While its reach far exceeds its grasp, for a Saturday night kind of movie, it's all right.
reviews.author: Preston Barta

reviews.text: Rocketman showcases Fletcher's ability to make the saying "shooting for the stars" a reality.
reviews.author: Michael Winkler

reviews.text: What the film lacks in originality within the biopic formula it makes up for in execution where, like the plasticine films of Ken Russell and Terry Gilliam, you never know when reality will burst at its seams.
reviews.author: Nathanael Hood

reviews.text: "Rocketman" wears its confidence in full sequin glory, and isn't afraid to take risks and reach for the stars. Taron Egerton is a perfect fit for this massive, corny, and grand biopic.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: "Rocketman" feels, in part, like Fletcher's effort to prove what he could do with a musical biography from scratch.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: Rocketman is, all in all, a well-made film, one that honors the fabulous man it's about at the very least from afar.
reviews.author: Matthew Dougherty

reviews.text: For me, Rocketman is a bit of history, a ton of laughs -- and a terrific musical.
reviews.author: Diana Saenger

reviews.text: Rocketman isn't just another biopic about a rock star whose music formed the soundtrack of a generation, it's an affirmation of the human endeavour - for all its good, and all its bad.
reviews.author: Katherine Monk

reviews.text: Rocketman has unusual dramatic heft for a jukebox musical, but that's a big curve on which to grade - the characters are still skin-deep.
reviews.author: David Edelstein

reviews.text: All and all, the words/music serve as the thread that binds Rocketman.
reviews.author: Wendy Shreve

reviews.text: It's soaring yet groundbound, joyous yet joyless, waggish yet wise; an enigma every bit as titillating as Sir. Elton John.
reviews.author: Asher Luberto

reviews.text: Thoroughly eye-popping, sprawling with vibrancy and vision, and spryly contemplative, ROCKETMAN is a virtual blast into the effervescent orbit of the meaningful musical biopic.
reviews.author: Frank Ochieng

reviews.text: ...lots of music, drugs, and gay sex...not just 'warts and all,' mostly just all warts...Unlike 'Bohemian Rhapsody,' it does not pull its punches.
reviews.author: Tony Medley

reviews.text: The best pop star biopic of the 21st Century.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: Saved from its chock-a-block narrative impatience by the pure puppy-ness of Taron Egerton's performance as Reg Dwight grown big and awful, rocketing toward twenty-eight years of sobriety.
reviews.author: Ray Pride

reviews.text: Just about every familiar note is here, from "Benny & the Jets" to "Your Song," with a slew of flashy production numbers highlighted by "Saturday Night's Alright" and "The Bitch Is Back."
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: Combines the best parts of Bohemian Rhapsody, the best and worst parts of Elton John's life and a great directorial vision to create a really entertaining whole.
reviews.author: Dan Murrell

reviews.text: Go for the music, go for Taron Egerton, stay for the supporting cast and the knowledge you gain...
reviews.author: Kristian Harloff

reviews.text: Rocketman [integrates Elton] John's music into the story in a way that reinvigorates the genre and renders his oeuvre insightfully personal.
reviews.author: Annlee Ellingson

reviews.text: Rocketman doesn't hide the dark sides of a life because it understands that all life has those moments. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alejandro G. Calvo

reviews.text: Rocketman never quite finds the wild momentum its characters seem to chase around in all those musical numbers.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Bloomer

reviews.text: There is nothing timid about the storytelling. Which is exactly how it should be, because this is the life of an extraordinary singer and showman.
reviews.author: Anupama Chopra

reviews.text: Thanks to imaginative musical numbers that aren't always bound by the limits of reality and the irrefutable charisma of its leading man,  Rocketman manages to break the mold just enough to stand tall above many of the genre's other offerings.
reviews.author: Brent Hankins

reviews.text: When done right, music biopics are enjoyable, foot-tapping celebrations of someone who gave magic to the world. Rocketman is done right.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: You feel the manic energy of Elton John coming alive whenever Taron dons outlandish costumes and belts one hit number after the other.
reviews.author: Devesh Sharma

reviews.text: Tiny Dancer is memorably reinvented as an ode to loneliness and alienation, while Goodbye Yellow Brick Road becomes a tale of anger, fear and desperation as Elton hits rock bottom.
reviews.author: David 'Mad Dog' Bradley

reviews.text: Fletcher is one of the few directors working today who really knows how to stage this sort of lavish musical number for the camera.
reviews.author: David Stratton

reviews.text: "Rocketman" has no problem blasting off and staying in a highly entertaining, if familiar, orbit. (Full Content Review for Parents - Sex, Profanity, etc. - also Available)
reviews.author: Jim Judy

reviews.text: The film traces how a shy piano prodigy named Reginald Dwight became the flamboyant showman, rock star and gay icon. Taron Egerton as Elton is outstanding.
reviews.author: Rashid Irani

reviews.text: From the high octane flourish and pomp of his stage persona, to the broken-hearted man who has been told he would never find true love, Taron plays Elton as a star and a human being with equal sincerity.
reviews.author: Soumya Srivastava

reviews.text: Unlike Bohemian Rhapsody, the new Elton John biopic is less beholden to clichés and doesn't feel the need to soft-pedal the fact that its protagonist is gay.
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: Rocketman raises the bar of what can be achieved in a musical biography with brilliant performances, particularly by Taron Egerton, and an unflinching look into Elton John's rockstar life.
reviews.author: Neil Soans

reviews.text: Rocketman isn't the best possible version of itself, but it does have the best possible man cast at its center.
reviews.author: Nick Johnston

reviews.text: How wonderful life is when you're in Rocketman's world.
reviews.author: Pat Mullen

reviews.text: Fletcher refreshes genre cliches with storytelling strategies that turn Rocketman into an infectiously energetic look at the life of a rock star.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: Rocketman is an unapologetic jukebox musical, using songs out of order to heighten the emotional weight of an otherwise chronological and fairly familiar story of success, oblivion, and redemption.
reviews.author: Stephen Garrett

reviews.text: The biopic about gay rock icon Elton John is proudly queer, packed with spectacle, and-though streaked with trauma and tragedy-radiant with joy.
reviews.author: Kristy Puchko

reviews.text: Bohemian Rhapsody this is not.
reviews.author: Gregory Wakeman

reviews.text: Dexter Fletcher's supple musical fantasy more akin to a stage play than biopic uses set pieces that flow into one another, tightly and brilliantly episodic, skipping from one eye-popping paragraph to the next.
reviews.author: Anne Brodie

reviews.text: The film's fantasy elements help elevate the by-the-numbers rock star trajectory, but the disappointing execution lacks the flamboyance that would better suit Elton's life story.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: Dazzling musical numbers, sets and costumes sparkle on the big screen in a biopic that truly captivates.
reviews.author: Roger Tennis

reviews.text: In its delight to bounce off the wall is where we find Rocketman's charm, intellect, and warmth.
reviews.author: Michael Arbeiter

reviews.text: Rocketman is giving me Moulin Rouge yumminess with Elton John at the forefront! Taron Egerton is fantabulous and splendidly singing all the Elton John hits you know and love! The outrageous costumes and musical narrative make it ripe for Broadway.
reviews.author: Carla Renata

reviews.text: Egerton's depiction of this charismatic character is infused with eclectic electricity. He does all his own singing. EJ said not to copy him too much but make the songs his own - and he has done so.
reviews.author: Barry Paris

reviews.text: One character advises an up-and-coming John to "kill the person you were born to be." John does, but lucky for us, he's reborn. In the end, he's "Still Standing," and thanks to "Rocketman," Egerton's career is about to last a long, long time.
reviews.author: Dana Barbuto

reviews.text: [Dexter] Fletcher's film could have provided more depth rather than rely on its grandiose Broadway musical sheen, but the sheen fits the subject, and it's unlikely anyone will be disappointed with the results.
reviews.author: Josh Terry

reviews.text: Taron Egerton...gives a dynamic, dazzling tour-de-force performance as Elton John.
reviews.author: Michael Ward

reviews.text: Not a fan of the genre and not a fan of Elton John but this movie takes old, stale songs and an old, stale rocker and makes both him and his music fresh again. I loved it.
reviews.author: Gary Wolcott

reviews.text: The filmmakers seek to delve deeper than appearances to highlight the existential struggle behind [his] choices.﻿ This isn't our perception of Elton John's life. It's his.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: It so often achieves in exhibiting Elton's fantasy that any doubt of fan approval can be put to rest, even if the legend's story gets lost within his own sparkling glamor.
reviews.author: Luke Parker

reviews.text: There's plenty to admire about both Taron Egerton and Hollywood's latest musical biopic. So why aren't we cheering like we should?
reviews.author: Christian Toto

reviews.text: The pop icon is vividly brought to life in this kaleidoscopic biopic.
reviews.author: Max Weiss

reviews.text: Unlike Rami Malek, Egerton actually sings in Rocketman, and while his voice is not a replica of John's, it is soulful enough to actually be convincing.
reviews.author: Alan Zilberman

reviews.text: "Rocketman" features high-energy musical numbers and some bleak moments - which one expects from a story of Elton John's life. But even with all the fantasy elements in this look at the larger-than-life performer, the pure, emotional scenes stand out.
reviews.author: Gary M. Kramer

reviews.text: Rocketman is the kind of music-biz biopic in which the star of the show, Elton John, sings a duet with his nine-year-old self...
reviews.author: Kurt Loder

reviews.text: While so many similar films get lost in their subject's importance... Rocketman hangs onto its humanity by highlighting Elton's journey to self-discovery.
reviews.author: Kyle Pinion

reviews.text: Rocketman should be considered less as a dramatic re-enactment than as a feat of creative license.
reviews.author: Blake Goble

reviews.text: A biopic in denial that it's a musical.
reviews.author: Cameron Williams

reviews.text: Parts of the film follows a formula that's a bit off key with the rest, and the otherwise well-paced and effervescent film drags. It comes a point where the predictability sets in, but Egerton's performance is what keeps the rhythm.
reviews.author: James Clay

reviews.text: Taron Egerton delivers a flawless performance and steers clear of attempting to mimic Elton.
reviews.author: Rebecca Murray

reviews.text: It may not deliver on the truly cosmic fantasia it swings for, but the swing itself is something, to be sure.
reviews.author: Conor O'Donnell

reviews.text: If you need somebody to recount the rise of a British rock god from pallid suburbia to the baroque extremes of fame, and to create a stir without causing too much of a fuss, Fletcher is your man.
reviews.author: Anthony Lane

reviews.text: Taron Egerton strongly commands this sparkling, colorful and moving journey to the musical universe of Elton John. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rene Sanchez

reviews.text: Whatever this movie's blunders, it succeeds because of two big selling points: the songs are just as catchy as they were in 1973, and Elton John is splendidly incarnated by Taron Egerton.
reviews.author: Robert Horton

reviews.text: Taron Egerton sets the bar for Best Actor of 2019 with his electric, transformative portrayal of Elton John...a rockin' celebration of a living-legend.
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: Taron Egerton's transformation into Elton John is a sight to behold in a film bursting with creativity, and sequins.
reviews.author: Dustin Chase

reviews.text: In real life, Elton John is not only a great songwriter and showman; he is a survivor. But the celebratory final moments of Rocketman can't compensate for the often-dreary narrative that leads up to them
reviews.author: Leonard Maltin

reviews.text: While Elton John's life may not have always been a fantasy, Taron Egerton has humanized and lionized him at the same time. Rocketman takes Egerton's star to new heights.
reviews.author: Linda and Al Lerner

reviews.text: We see the energy and magnetism of Sir Elton as a performer, and as the person, vulnerable, scared, and longing to be truly accepted.
reviews.author: Nell Minow

reviews.text: The quest for a great musician biopic continues, but Rocketman is a half-step up the keyboard.
reviews.author: Sean Collier

reviews.text: Rocketman is more akin to a stage musical, chockablock with wild, fantastical numbers and intricate choreography.
reviews.author: Steve Katz

reviews.text: The story reshuffles reality, especially time and facts, and the film is more enjoyable for it.
reviews.author: Leah Pickett

reviews.text: [Taron] Egerton swirls in the beautiful rhythms of Rocketman, complementing its unapologetic embrace of everything that made Reggie Dwight become the beloved Elton John in the first place.
reviews.author: Andrea Thompson

reviews.text: Let's not pretend the film is anything but a tribute to a life well-lived, one filled with flash, dash, and cash.
reviews.author: Michael Calleri

reviews.text: An irresistible and simply marvelous film. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Juanma Fernández París

reviews.text: Fletcher isn't seeking to reinvent a very practiced storytelling formula; he's just perfecting it.
reviews.author: David Sims

reviews.text: I forgive Rocketman many of its screenplay sins because of Egerton, the direction and those damn catchy tunes.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: Although the movie will be rightfully and enthusiastically embraced by the singer's fans, it has something to offer those with no more than a casual recognition and appreciation of the man's music.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: Rocketman grows exhausting by the end...
reviews.author: Kristen Yoonsoo Kim

reviews.text: A musical fantasy that never quite breaks free from the rock-biopic formula but nonetheless delivers some satisfying pizzazz and joy.
reviews.author: Anita Katz

reviews.text: The songs, the color, the dancing and, yes, the redemption are all intended to make people happy. And will.
reviews.author: John Anderson

reviews.text: With flourishes of great rock movies such as The Who's Tommy and even Alan Parker's Pink Floyd: The Wall, Rocketman tells John's story stylistically, with emotional depth and has the benefit of possessing a memorable soundtrack from the start.
reviews.author: George M. Thomas

reviews.text: It is not just the music and performances that are worth a celebratory jig in the aisle. What also refreshes in this look at the wilder days of Elton John is the way it unapologetically settles scores.
reviews.author: Alison Rowat

reviews.text: This dizzy, delirious jukebox musical has the energy and visual dynamism to truly reflect the outlandish aesthetic and performance style of its subject.
reviews.author: Katie Walsh

reviews.text: Which is to say that as long as "Rocketman" is charting the jet-propelled rise of Elton John in the early 1970s, it is an absolute gas.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: It's an old story, but true in its own way, and Fletcher and Egerton find ways to give these familiar ideas a humor and over-the-top energy appropriate to its subject.
reviews.author: Gary Thompson

reviews.text: "Rocketman" is as weird, brazen and stylish as the man at its center.
reviews.author: Chris Hewitt

reviews.text: Elton John is a legend, there's no question. No one can take issue with his colorful life being given the biopic treatment. The execution here, however, is another story.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: Before seeing Rocketman, I had absolutely zero interest in Elton John or his music. After seeing it, I just can't stop listening to his music with new ears, and I can't wait to see Rocketman a second, third and fourth time.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: While 'Rocketman' disappoints in many respects...it does offer a cavalcade of many of John's greatest hits-even if in attenuated form and incongruous context-and for fans of the singer that may be enough.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: In marrying the music and the biographical tale with such care, the film transcends the gimmicky conceit of the jukebox musical...
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: Energetic, imaginative musical numbers... The way Fletcher incorporates music and emotion into the story should be instructive to anyone making a rock biopic hereafter.
reviews.author: Eric D. Snider

reviews.text: Egerton is commanding throughout. His performance is truly a marvel. "Rocketman" as well.
reviews.author: Soren Andersen

reviews.text: This is rock storytelling as entertainment, not a social chronicle like Woodstock or Gimme Shelter.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: One side of the Sir Elton John story: clichéd, weirdly canted, still largely enjoyable.
reviews.author: Daniel Eagan

reviews.text: Regardless of whether it secures the appropriate huzzahs and awards, Rocketman is a cinematic, artistic and musical success anchored by a stunning lead performance.
reviews.author: Tom Fitzgerald and Lorenzo Marquez

reviews.text: This movie elevates itself above regular jukebox musicals because it understands its subject and the music, leading to just some brilliant sequences.
reviews.author: Terence Johnson

reviews.text: Egerton's electric performance as the famed rock star drives this jukebox musical.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: Director Dexter Fletcher... bills this as a "true fantasy." The fiction may be upfront -- composite characters cannot sue -- but it's awfully familiar.
reviews.author: Richard von Busack

reviews.text: A proper rock biopic.
reviews.author: Jeremy Jahns

reviews.text: In a pop landscape littered with tragic early deaths, Egerton captures the spirit behind the still-standing star, and leaves you with an optimism that lingers a long, long time.
reviews.author: Dana Kennedy

reviews.text: The easy thing to do is hone an impression, but Egerton digs in deeper and finds the man inside the costume.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: Starring the overly strenuous Taron Egerton, Rocketman is a campy, overblown, self-glorifying fantasia.
reviews.author: Peter Rainer

reviews.text: Egerton does a phenomenal job... His performance is an emotional rollercoaster of extreme highs and lows, but is always underpinned by a heartbreaking wish for true acceptance and love.
reviews.author: Carl Kozlowski

reviews.text: Credit must be given to [director Dexter] Fletcher for bringing in a lot of ideas. Unfortunately, just about none of them are good ones.
reviews.author: Kyle Smith

reviews.text: A cathartic outpouring of a lifetime's load of hurts and grudges. Fortunately for us, it's expressed in some of the most exuberant pop songs ever produced and it's lavishly adorned with stardust and sequins.
reviews.author: Sandra Hall

reviews.text: A coke-fuelled musical odyssey beyond the black and white.
reviews.author: Cameron Frew

reviews.text: Rocketman sticks to the hits, avoiding any unexpected B-sides in soundtrack or story, but as a jukebox musical, it's a fun effort.
reviews.author: Roe McDermott

reviews.text: Less a warts 'n all life story than a gorgeous collage of music videos, the film is propelled by the magnetic performance by Taron Egerton as one of rock's greatest showmen.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: A wildly entertaining (if a bit unwieldy) story of how Elton John went from neglected kid to outrageous, hit-making rock star.
reviews.author: Mara Reinstein

reviews.text: This is one musical adventure that shoots for the stars, and succeeds on nearly every single level.
reviews.author: JimmyO

reviews.text: uses John and Taupin's songs to dramatize various important stages of his life, usually ending in a completely different time and space where they begin. The effect is dazzling...a heady rush of entertainment with an emotional undertow.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: A tightly packed, superbly mounted, decidedly barbed valentine...In keeping with the tradition of the best musicals, the song-and-dance scenes form an intrinsic part of the story [and] brim with creativity, energy and deliciously indulgent camera work.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: Rocketman offers everything that we want in a well-crafted biopic musical of Sir Elton John from the show-stopping numbers to the costume changes.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: Dexter Fletcher makes your basic Freudian gin and tonic... with a showstopping crowd pleaser.
reviews.author: Robert Daniels

reviews.text: "Rocketman" has the pleasing aesthetic of a storybook jukebox musical but is punctuated with a piercing and unescapable sense of melancholy.
reviews.author: Matthew Passantino

reviews.text: Mostly I loved the creative vision of Rocketman. It was new and vibrant and had me grinning from ear to ear
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: The ultimate Elton John movie musical Rocketman gets liftoff from a sensational performance by Taron Egerton.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: Rocketman feels slightly like a missed opportunity to dig a little deeper into the life and humanity of a person who has earned his place in the pop cultural firmament.
reviews.author: Todd Gilchrist

reviews.text: The Elton John biopic is as fabulous, flamboyant, and fun as its legendary subject deserves.
reviews.author: Kevin Fallon

reviews.text: John's songs chased such massive emotional crescendos that they risked collapsing onto themselves at every turn. When the movie takes a similar risk, it just feels right.
reviews.author: Norman Wilner

reviews.text: Loud and colorful, with the dynamic camerawork injecting another layer of excitement and joy.
reviews.author: Sean Keane

reviews.text: Rocketman is a fun, poignant rhinestone of a movie that proves that a musical biopic can be a powerful force - if done right.
reviews.author: Anne Cohen

reviews.text: The best full-on musical phantasmagoria about a famous person destroying and reclaiming their life since Bob Fosse's All That Jazz.
reviews.author: Andrew Parker

reviews.text: It's whimsy, magic and metaphor.
reviews.author: Brad Wheeler

reviews.text: As debauched and kaleidoscopic as the life it portrays, Rocketman is truly thrilling experience.
reviews.author: Kim Hughes

reviews.text: [Taron Egerton] is an, at times, mesmeric presence, drawing the audience in and taking them on this sometimes crazy fantasy.
reviews.author: James Croot

reviews.text: Rocketman is a genuinely enjoyable bit of nostalgic myth-making.
reviews.author: Kelly Vance

reviews.text: Because of its many other virtues, Rocketman can be forgiven for using that worn out, used up device of telling the story via rehab group therapy sessions.
reviews.author: Lisa Johnson Mandell

reviews.text: What's odd, considering John's flair for the flamboyant, is that the film is bare-bones and brutally honest, even as it's full of allegory and metaphor.
reviews.author: Chuck Yarborough

reviews.text: The story told between the tunes in Rocketman never achieves takeoff.
reviews.author: Leigh Paatsch

reviews.text: It helps that Egerton so masterfully rises to the challenge of inhabiting the role in ways that go beyond a certain more-than-passing physical resemblance to the man or the fact that he does his own singing and handles the choreography with ease.
reviews.author: Ed Masley

reviews.text: A likable movie about a likable music man, though it falls short in obvious comparisons to Bohemian Rhapsody, a better film about a better singer.
reviews.author: Christopher Lloyd

reviews.text: Joyful and rowdy, self-deprecating and vulnerable, absolutely electrifying as it deconstructs the sex-drugs-and-rock'n'-roll story. Taron Egerton is chills-inducingly good. Sheer cinematic magic.
reviews.author: MaryAnn Johanson

reviews.text: It is, gloriously, the most.
reviews.author: Simon Miraudo

reviews.text: A poignant yet preposterous journey that's equal parts campy and cordial, but never less than inherently entertaining.
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: After threatening to go full Walk Hard (one of the best film criticisms in movie form), it deviates enough from the formula to become interesting enough to deserve a recommendation. [Full review in Portuguese]
reviews.author: Pablo Villaça

reviews.text: While the chronological progression still holds Rocketman on a familiar narrative path, the film's ambition concerning the incorporation of fantastical musical sequences makes it a memorable and engaging watch.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: Rocketman gets nearly everything right; the directing flourishes with style, Taron Egerton is committed, vulnerable, and self-destructive, the music carries purpose, and it's inspiring to anyone that has ever felt broken or defeated by an addiction
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: Now this is my idea of a rock star biography. Flamboyant and fun, featuring dramatically aligned hit musical numbers, this toe-tapper never forgets the complicated soul of its you-thought-you-knew-him subject.
reviews.author: Joanna Langfield

reviews.text: More sincere than Bohemian Rhapsody. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Irene Crespo

reviews.text: The young, gay, conflicted and addicted Elton John is brought to life by an electrifying, Oscar-caliber Taron Egerton and Dexter Fletcher's dazzling cinematic inventiveness. Forget the cliches, this one you don't want to miss.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: Rocketman is a shimmering love letter to the Pinball Wizard that mixes its pop jukebox with pop psychology. It's no deeper than either, but it really does pop.
reviews.author: David Crow

reviews.text: The point of "Rocketman" isn't self-aggrandizement. It's fan service of an especially and characteristically generous kind.
reviews.author: A.O. Scott

reviews.text: As someone who had their doubts about the movie, Rocketman's unapologetic nature about Elton John is exactly the kind of movie I wanted.
reviews.author: Rachel Leishman

reviews.text: Rocketman is a fun, trippy hallucinogen.
reviews.author: Dwight Brown

reviews.text: As much as "Rocketman" reminds of just how many outstanding songs Elton John has recorded, it also digs into the pain and emotion that lie within those toe-tapping treasures.
reviews.author: Brian Truitt

reviews.text: I think it's gonna be a long long time until we see another music biopic as tremendous as Rocketman.
reviews.author: Simon Thompson

reviews.text: Egerton gives a performance with such thrills and vulnerability, such charisma and pathos, that it's hard not to be wowed.
reviews.author: Christy Lemire

reviews.text: A glittery goblet of tribute, a rollicking twist on rock biopics, and a stupendously inventive musical with a star-making performance by Egerton, who fills it with pitch-perfect performances.
reviews.author: Neil Pond

reviews.text: With elaborate dance numbers that have a CGI-added "All That Jazz" feel, the movie is part rags-to-riches story and part rock concert.
reviews.author: Jason Guerrasio

reviews.text: If Malek could win an Oscar for doing an impersonation, then Egerton deserves 10 Oscars, a purple heart, a Nobel Peace Prize, and be knighted for delivering a PERFORMANCE.
reviews.author: Rendy Jones

reviews.text: Fletcher, Egerton, et al have managed to create a memorable film filled with all the outrageousness, drama, fun and entertainment deserving of the global superstar known as Sir Elton John.
reviews.author: Jeanne Kaplan

reviews.text: A fun, self-serving, sing-a-long-able romp that is at its best when it's being as much a diva as its subject.
reviews.author: Katie Parker

reviews.text: a film that treats narrative segues as unique entertainment propositions, merging time and space with fussy panache, rendering the past as a kind of phantasmagoric pageant
reviews.author: Luke Buckmaster

reviews.text: The spirit of the song guides the staging with an ability to match its brilliance. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Luis Martínez

reviews.text: ...contains an emotional truth that will likely resonate with you for a long, long time.
reviews.author: Pauline Adamek

reviews.text: [T]his is a film that hits you like a ton of bricks.Yellow road-building ones, naturally.
reviews.author: Matthew Bond

reviews.text: Rocketman's flamboyant superficiality may be its saving grace.
reviews.author: Tom Shone

reviews.text: Often, it feels like we're watching two biopics at the same time, but both are handled with such confidence and skill that it's rare for the viewer to be able to spot the join.
reviews.author: Terry Staunton

reviews.text: 'Rocketman' is a glitzy, fantastical, sequin-drenched spectacle, wisely juxtaposed by the bleak and destructive toll that comes from a life of unfettered excess.
reviews.author: Doug Jamieson

reviews.text: Camouflaged under appropriately diminishing hair, flamboyant spectacles and outrageous costumes, Taron Egerton's superb lead performance offers Rocketman every chance to soar but the film is a mixed bag.
reviews.author: Louise Keller

reviews.text: For me, Fletcher is the real star of this show, a director whose enthusiasm for musical storytelling shines through every frame, hitting all the emotional high notes. I have yet to come down.
reviews.author: Mark Kermode

reviews.text: It's a shiny, sterile, generic wannabe musical biopic that clearly values truisms over substance, and even the style isn't enough to make it worth watching.
reviews.author: Luke Hicks

reviews.text: A joyous and boisterous fantasy grounded in reality and truth. Taron Egerton and Jamie Bell have wonderful chemistry; costume designer Julian Day has created a symphony of spangles.
reviews.author: Sarah Cartland

reviews.text: Rocketman manages to be campy and yet sincere, serious and yet ridiculous, profound and yet silly, and quite wonderful. Just like Elton himself.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: Rocketman is the film that will finally get Taron Egerton the recognition he deserves as a wildly talented actor.
reviews.author: Ashley Menzel

reviews.text: A crowd-pleasing film, but one that clings to convention in a way that makes its story feel that much more muted and small.
reviews.author: Adam Lubitow

reviews.text: Glittery, glam rock musical soars; expect sex and drugs.
reviews.author: Joyce Slaton

reviews.text: An uneven combination of strong performances, an insightful script (by Lee Hall) and iffy musical numbers, "Rocketman" is inventive and enjoyable, even when it teeters unsteadily on the platform heels of its own ambition.
reviews.author: Rafer Guzman

reviews.text: it's an orgy of clothes, cars, mansions and um, orgies
reviews.author: Chris Hunneysett

reviews.text: Rocketman features a stunning, powerful star turn from Taron Egerton as Elton John in a sharp and entertaining jukebox musical-style biopic.
reviews.author: Molly Freeman

reviews.text: Fletcher and his star Taron Egerton fling themselves flamboyantly into John's life, riffing on events, giving them a surreal spin but always keeping how John is feeling about each moment front and centre.
reviews.author: Amber Wilkinson

reviews.text: There may be a showbiz biopic to come that matches Rocketman for wit, energy, charm, candour and shameless exuberance. But I think it's gonna be a long, long time.
reviews.author: Matthew Norman

reviews.text: Finally, someone - Bohemian Rhapsody director Dexter Fletcher - has dared to make a movie about a flamboyant, original singer which is actually flamboyant and original.
reviews.author: Grant Rollings

reviews.text: 1st act is very strong & Egerton is extremely talented. So while this only scratches the surface of Elton John, it's a good intro to the icon, even if a bit "by the numbers".
reviews.author: Grace Randolph

reviews.text: There's a lot of Technicolor flair in Dexter Fletcher's flamboyant study of Elton John - and a beating heart in... Taron Egerton's portrayal of an artist whose prodigious talent was matched only by his personal demons and a desperate hunger for love.
reviews.author: Leah Greenblatt

reviews.text: Just as dispiriting as these cheesy platitudes is the fact that, beat by beat, the film follows the same trajectory as virtually every other movie ever made about a musician...
reviews.author: Giovanni Marchini Camia

reviews.text: [Taron Egerton] truly blasts off in Rocketman. A performance so rich and colorful that it wows and captures the very soul of Elton John; a man we have all loved from afar.
reviews.author: Jay Dasgupta

reviews.text: As the film has it, music courses through every fibre of Elton's being, and these big show-stopping moments are a fun way of letting us understand the power music held over him...
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: Taron Egerton is absolutely electric as Elton John in Dexter Fletcher's imaginative, brash and dazzling musical biopic of the legendary musician.
reviews.author: Erik Anderson

reviews.text: Rocketman is dazzling! Dexter Fletcher and Taron Egerton are proving to be a standout filmmaking duo. The music and fantasy elements are staggeringly enchanting, and the movie also delivers a deeply moving exploration of isolation and forgiveness.
reviews.author: Perri Nemiroff

reviews.text: Two pictures are contained here: Egerton's lived-in universe of glammy woe and Fletcher's pedestrian take on musical theater. The one with passion is most memorable. The one with the hits dominates the run time.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: [Egerton] captures the Elton-ness of Elton without ever resorting to mimicry, and he does his own singing which, astonishingly, also captures the Elton-ness of Elton.
reviews.author: Deborah Ross

reviews.text: If you're looking for truth, you'll get some, but what Rocketman bestows is more than truth. It's pure musical wonder.
reviews.author: Douglas Davidson

reviews.text: As a singer Egerton lands somewhere between Elton John and William Hung, but regardless he feels the words deeply and has so much charisma that his red blood cells may well be sequins.
reviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski

reviews.text: By making Rocketman an actual musical, it avoids some of the Dewey Cox biopic formula.
reviews.author: Fred Topel

reviews.text: Its commitment to tell its story in such an inventive and entertaining way has to be applauded.
reviews.author: Reuben Baron

reviews.text: Egerton delivers the songs without lapsing into parody and the tragicomic tone really does capture the absurdity and sheer artistry of one of the most impressive pop performers of all time.
reviews.author: Alan Corr

reviews.text: You can't simplify a person's entire motivation into a few relics from childhood, as [Dexter] Fletcher clumsily attempts here. But when we hurtle through a life lived, and when John interacts with his past, Rocketman becomes a hot-blooded joy.
reviews.author: Ben Flanagan

reviews.text: Oozing with moments of high camp and of utter euphoric joy, Rocketman does a great job in capitalising on John's impressive back catalogue of catchy rock anthems to give us one of the greatest rock biopics of the decade.
reviews.author: Linda Marric

reviews.text: The spirit of Elton John oozes from every frame of this candid journey through his tumultuous career, even when it regrettably bows to tired genre conventions.
reviews.author: Jennifer Heaton

reviews.text: Rocketman feels precisely as cynical as Elton's mawkish John Lewis advert: an extension of the same endless, needless and unremarkable one-man marketing campaign.
reviews.author: Ali Gray

reviews.text: Rocketman takes risks that pay off in a movie that's as colourful, complicated, creative and larger than life as its subject.
reviews.author: Rosie Fletcher

reviews.text: Crushingly literal... More redolent of a Christmas round-robin letter than of anything resembling cinema.
reviews.author: Ryan Gilbey

reviews.text: Because the film is a cartoon bus, we don't care if the road is often familiar.
reviews.author: Nigel Andrews

reviews.text: A lot of fun and very cute.
reviews.author: Angie Errigo

reviews.text: A triumphant film from Dexter Fletcher, with a star performance from Taron Egerton. Warts and all - this is easily one of the films of the year.
reviews.author: Jo-Ann Titmarsh

reviews.text: As an origin story - and period biopic - Rocketman does justice, with an appropriate panache, to the early years of a bonafide music legend.
reviews.author: Tori Brazier

reviews.text: Whatever the film's shortfall in psychodynamics, Rocketman invokes the spirit and specifics of music -- enormously aided by Mr. Egerton's performance -- to illuminate the hero's soul.
reviews.author: Joe Morgenstern

reviews.text: It becomes a character study of how fame and fortune mean so little when your personal life is a wreck.
reviews.author: Kaleem Aftab

reviews.text: Rocketman is a real winner with a career-defining performance from Taron Egerton as Elton John, and it proves Fletcher still has it.
reviews.author: Maria Lattila

reviews.text: (mostly) distract us from its superficiality.
reviews.author: Pat Brown

reviews.text: Pure Elton [John], and pure pleasure.
reviews.author: Anna Smith

reviews.text: Like its flamboyant subject, it's a movie outfitted to the nines in dazzle and verve, even if it's gotten all dressed up with nowhere to go but the most conventional places.
reviews.author: Jake Coyle

reviews.text: Rocketman has the feel of a showstopper Broadway musical. Lightning does indeed strike twice for director Dexter Fletcher. It's a wild ride, squarely on the shoulders of Taron Egerton.
reviews.author: Julian Roman

reviews.text: As inventive as the movie gets in teasing out both the melancholy and the joy of John and Taupin's songs, Rocketman still genuflects toward the myth of biopic respectability.
reviews.author: Jesse Hassenger

reviews.text: It is a crowdpleaser with all the lyrics, full of emotional peaks, with interpretations (point for Egerton) of 20 of the most popular themes of Elton John's career. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Diego Batlle

reviews.text: A correct and effective product, those that hook you without you noticing. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Luis Caviaro

reviews.text: "Rocketman" does not purport to be much more than an elaborate work of spectacle, jam-packing 20 excerpted musical numbers into its two-hour runtime.
reviews.author: Caroline Tsai

reviews.text: Rocketman is magnificent and ridiculous, a feathered melanage of clichés and originality, of respectful homage and unrepentant nostalgia.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: Annoyingly hyperactive, familiar but decently entertaining
reviews.author: Jordan Ruimy

reviews.text: Regal showmanship fuels Rocketman's mission, propelling the rousing, heartfelt musical to gleeful heights.
reviews.author: Ella Kemp

reviews.text: Rocket Man truly does soar
reviews.author: Jason Gorber

reviews.text: It's whenever the songs begin that the film truly finds its feet.
reviews.author: Karen Han

reviews.text: It's a satisfying and even rousing film at times, but it doesn't provide much enlightenment.
reviews.author: Richard Lawson

reviews.text: Rocketman sometimes feels like it's lost its way, especially near the end. But it's still a joyous celebration, a colorful story about love that can help people heal.
reviews.author: Alissa Wilkinson

reviews.text: It finds strength in texture, beauty in sadness, and an inspired finale in a crackpot arrangement of one of the singer's greatest hits.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: It's impossible not to listen to the music that John and Taupin made and not get swept away by the whole thing.
reviews.author: Mike Ryan

reviews.text: Ideally, a movie like this would either fully sweep its audience up in a rush of emotion or else take them out of their comfort zones. Rocketman does neither.
reviews.author: Manuela Lazic

reviews.text: The thing is an absolute hoot.
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: A dense jukebox musical variation on A Christmas Carol...
reviews.author: Eric Kohn

reviews.text: Rocketman aspires to nothing more than colourful reportage of a life already well-known to the public, dissolving into an encyclopedia entry as the final title cards inform us that things turned out alright for this "Elton John" fellow.
reviews.author: Charles Bramesco

reviews.text: A rock star origin story that flaunts its hero's superpowers as if he were the newest member of the Avengers, "Rocketman" is shameless in its ambitions to crown Elton John as one of music's greatest artists, most fascinating figures and saddest souls.
reviews.author: Tim Grierson

reviews.text: Taron Egerton, in a fantastic performance, doesn't impersonate Elton John, he becomes him; he doesn't lip-sync, he sings, making the songs matter in that moment in the story.
reviews.author: David Sexton

reviews.text: The result is a far more honest-feeling depiction of the stratospheric highs and cavernous lows of one of our greatest musical minds, with a never-better Egerton wearing his heart on his sleeve throughout.
reviews.author: Jordan Farley

reviews.text: A sequin-encrusted delight. On paper it reads like a by-the-book biopic; on screen it explodes with the kind of colour and energy that only Elton John himself could invoke.
reviews.author: John Nugent

reviews.text: As with its beloved subject and his enormous catalog of multiplatinum earworms, the movie's familiarity turns out to be crucial to its charm.
reviews.author: Justin Chang

reviews.text: Fletcher stages the musical numbers with real panache, and Egerton is commanding on stage.
reviews.author: James Mottram

reviews.text: The songs explode from the screen, time jumps catapult the story forward with exhilarating élan and even the emotional stuff lands, for the most part.
reviews.author: Philip De Semlyen

reviews.text: Whatever you think of Sir Elton John, Rocketman unashamedly invites us to celebrate the fact that... he's still standing.
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: Rocketman has everything to be a hit and maintains part of the structure of Bohemian Rhapsody although it is much more sincere. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pablo O. Scholz

reviews.text: Dexter Fletcher has fashioned an ebullient monument to pop superstar Elton John - featuring a likable turn from Taron Egerton in the lead role - that's clichéd in the telling, but gets by on the strength of his early catalog.
reviews.author: Peter Debruge

reviews.text: It's largely to the credit of star Taron Egerton, who leans fearlessly into the role's wild excesses, that the movie remains airborne.
reviews.author: David Rooney

reviews.text: Taron is an incredible screen force with endless charisma and charm, it's no wonder Elton was adamant he should take on the role.
reviews.author: Halina Watts

reviews.text: [Director Dexter] Fletcher films even the darkest scenes in a very flamboyant fashion and manages to leaven matters with some ironic humour.
reviews.author: Geoffrey Macnab

reviews.text: Dexter Fletcher's fabulous Elton John musical is a heart-racing, toe-tapping, all-glitter-cannons-blazing triumph...
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: Rocketman is an honest, heartfelt tribute to Elton John's music and his public image.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: This has best picture nominee written all over it.
reviews.author: Dan Wootton

synopsis: Young Reginald Dwight changes his name to Elton John and collaborates with singer-songwriter Bernie Taupin to become one of the most iconic figures in pop history. Set to his most beloved songs, it's the epic musical story of Elton John, his breakthrough years in the 1970s and his fantastical transformation from shy piano prodigy to international superstar.
